chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Start of Tape 3, studios compared
summary: Tape 3 begins; McRae continues comparing Decca and Brunswick studios with RCA's 23rd Street studio.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Oh, (inaudible), yeah. Decca sound and the Brunswick sound too. You must remember that Decca -- those studios like that -- 50 West 52nd Street -- they didn't have the studios that RCA Victor had. RCA Victor had -- they only had down 23rd Street. That was considered one of the (inaudible) terrific studios there. We've recorded there. I eventually recorded down there when I took (inaudible). I hadn't been there since I did some things for the... Well, you know, I think I did some things for Fats Waller down there years ago. But I don't think that they usually -- See, a lot of those dates that would go in there -- you do a lot of those dates -- they never kept track of some of the musicians that they use on those dates. Some of those things that Fats Waller would go in there and do right quick, you know, and come out.
